_comment: broadcast is registered in op_defs/basic_ops/xccl_ops.py and had no workload file
anywhere in the repo, so it was untested rather than unsupported -- on both
Worth having rather than filler: broadcast is the one collective whose cost model
differs from the other four. all_reduce, all_gather, reduce_scatter and all_to_all
all move O(size) per rank and their bus_size grows with rank count; a broadcast
moves the same bytes to every rank from one source, so a ring implementation is
(n-1) sequential hops of the whole payload and a tree is log(n) of it. That makes
it the case where the algorithm choice shows up most plainly in the number -- and
on this instance algorithm choice is not free: a replica group whose chips are not
adjacent on the 4x4 torus falls back to the Mesh algorithm and is then capped at
40 MiB. Read this file's ws=8 rows against the ccl8_llm and topo_far8 labels.
In serving it is also not a synthetic op: it is how sampled token ids and any
rank-0 decision reach the other TP ranks, at tiny sizes where the latency floor
is the whole cost, which is why the small batch_size rows are kept.
dtype includes int8 for the same reason as p2p.json -- the int8 collective anomaly
was found on all_gather and all_to_all, and broadcast is a third algorithm.
